sections.title: The Earth is the Lord's
observations: This opening verse establishes God's sovereignty over all creation. It emphasizes that everything in the world, including its inhabitants, belongs to God. This is a foundational truth that undergirds the entire psalm and serves as a reminder of God's ultimate authority and ownership.
The phrase 'the fullness thereof' suggests that not only the land but everything within it—its resources, creatures, and people—are under God's dominion.

sections.title: Who Shall Ascend the Hill of the Lord?
observations: This section poses a rhetorical question about who is worthy to stand in God's presence. It highlights the moral and spiritual qualifications required to approach God, emphasizing purity of heart and hands.
The imagery of 'the hill of the Lord' refers to Mount Zion, symbolizing God's dwelling place. This signifies the importance of holiness and righteousness in our relationship with God.

sections.title: The King of Glory
observations: The psalm concludes with a triumphant declaration of God's majesty and power. It personifies God as the 'King of Glory,' inviting the gates to lift up and recognize His sovereignty.
This section serves as a reminder of God's strength and the reverence He commands. It encourages believers to acknowledge God's glory and to live in a manner that reflects His holiness.

importantVerses.commentary: The earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord, affirming His sovereignty.
The question of who can stand before God highlights the need for purity and righteousness.
Declaring God as the King of Glory emphasizes His majesty and power.

questions: What does it mean for the earth to belong to the Lord?
How can we prepare ourselves to stand in the presence of God?
In what ways can we recognize and honor God as the King of Glory in our daily lives?
